result.label: Source-read

claims.claim: An acknowledgment or promise must be in a writing signed by the party to be charged to serve as sufficient evidence of a new or continuing contract, subject to the payment rule stated next.
claims.quote: No acknowledgment or promise is sufficient evidence of a new or continuing contract, by which to take the case out of the operation of this title, unless the same is contained in some writing, signed by the party to be charged thereby,
claims.note: The draft states a necessary condition; it does not say that signing any writing restarts the period.

claims.claim: A payment by the party to be charged on principal or interest due on a promissory note is deemed a sufficient acknowledgment or promise of a continuing contract.
claims.quote: any payment on account of principal or interest due on a promissory note made by the party to be charged shall be deemed a sufficient acknowledgment or promise of a continuing contract
claims.note: The draft limits this rule to promissory notes rather than applying it to every written debt.

claims.claim: Each qualifying payment stops the running of the time to commence an action on the note and starts a new period.
claims.quote: to stop, from time to time as any such payment is made, the running of the time within which an action may be commenced upon the principal sum or upon any installment of principal or interest due on such note, and to start the running of a new period of time
claims.note: The statute describes actions for the principal sum or an installment of principal or interest.

claims.claim: Such a payment does not by itself revive a cause of action once barred.
claims.quote: but no such payment of itself shall revive a cause of action once barred.

claims.claim: The period for an action on a contract, obligation or liability founded on a written instrument is four years within the stated scope.
claims.quote:
Within four years:
(a) An action upon any contract, obligation or liability founded upon an instrument in writing, except as provided in Section 336a;
claims.note: The post-sale money-judgment proviso is outside the stated scope.

claims.claim: The four-year rule is subject to the exception in Section 336a.
Once the Section 337 period has run, a person may not bring suit or initiate arbitration or another legal proceeding to collect the debt.
claims.quote: When the period in which an action must be commenced under this section has run, a person shall not bring suit or initiate an arbitration or other legal proceeding to collect the debt.

claims.claim: The Section 337 period may be extended only pursuant to Section 360.
claims.quote: The period in which an action may be commenced under this section shall only be extended pursuant to Section 360.

result.summary: The provided texts support each claim within the stated scope. The draft distinguishes a promissory-note payment made while the period is running from one made after the claim is already barred.
